articles.title: Power and cooling limits push 100,000-accelerator AI clusters into scale-across networking
articles.excerpt: 📅 November 21, 2026 • Tom's Hardware, Chip Dispatch On November 20 at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), researchers from The Ohio State University described how high-performance networking evolves under ph…
articles.body: 📅 November 21, 2026 • Tom's Hardware, Chip Dispatch On November 20 at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), researchers from The Ohio State University described how high-performance networking evolves under physical pressure: power, cooling and space limits push AI compute beyond a single data center. The emerging answer is scale-across, a third networking domain connecting buildings, campuses and even regions into one performance target. Modern AI clusters typically hold more than 100,000 accelerators and potentially millions of CPU endpoints, and accelerator performance grows faster than communication capability, so network efficiency decides how well the cluster uses its compute. Networking splits into three domains .

articles.title: AI Coding Productivity in 2026: Building Got Cheap, Deciding Didn't
articles.excerpt: AI tools made building software cheaper and more common. The evidence on speed is mixed, and the cost of building the wrong thing has not moved. Here is what the 2025-2026 data actually says. AI codin…
articles.body: AI tools made building software cheaper and more common. The evidence on speed is mixed, and the cost of building the wrong thing has not moved. Here is what the 2025-2026 data actually says. AI coding productivity rose in reach more than in proven speed. In 2025, 84% of developers used or planned to use AI tools, yet METR's controlled trials found experienced developers 19% slower in early 2025 and only weak evidence of speed-up by late 2025. Meanwhile 43% of failed startups still cite poor product-market fit. Building got cheaper; knowing what to build did not. Key takeaways AI coding is now the default. 84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools, and 50.6% of professional developers use them daily ( Stack Overflow, 2025 ).

articles.body: Yonto Player is a media player for your own library on Android TV, phones and tablets. Its repo keeps its workflows as Markdown files that any AI coding agent, or a person, can follow. This post shows what that means in practice, because the format is small enough to copy. The repo has a skills/ directory with seven folders. Each holds one file, SKILL.md , and two of them add a references/ folder. There is one for a quality round, one for filing an issue, one for sweeping the issue queue, one for fixing a single issue, one for opening a pull request, one for a walkthrough of the app as a viewer, and one for writing a source plugin. The shape of a skill A skill has two parts. At the top is front matter with a name and a description .

Here is how to map stakeholders and use it. Stakeholder management for product managers is the work of keeping the people who shape or depend on your product informed, involved at the right level and aligned on decisions, without any formal authority over them. In 2026 the hard part has changed. Stakeholders arrive with AI-generated analysis, so a PM's advantage is no longer having more information. articles.title: MongoDB to Snowflake with Change Streams: A Hands-On Tutorial Without Kafka
articles.excerpt: A MongoDB to Snowflake pipeline usually starts as a script: mongoexport a collection to JSON, load the file, repeat tomorrow. It holds up until someone asks why a cancelled order is still in the wareh…
articles.body: A MongoDB to Snowflake pipeline usually starts as a script: mongoexport a collection to JSON, load the file, repeat tomorrow. It holds up until someone asks why a cancelled order is still in the warehouse. Documents are updated and deleted in place, and an export sees none of that as a change. The usual ways to move MongoDB data into Snowflake: Manual export: mongoexport to JSON, then COPY INTO a VARIANT column. You run a script and a scheduler, freshness is hours to daily, and every run is a full reload. Debezium, Kafka and the Snowflake Kafka connector: changes arrive within seconds, and deletes depend on the connector's tombstone handling. You operate Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium and a schema registry to get there.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
